_README: Error-level Codacy issues on main that are reviewed and accepted.
The gate in .github/workflows/codacy-alerts.yml fails when main carries an Error-level
issue that is NOT listed here. Anything listed needs a reason, and the list is meant to
shrink: this is the same contract as tests/html_sink_baseline.json.
Match is on (filePath, patternId, lineText) with whitespace collapsed. The line NUMBER is
deliberately not part of the key -- it moves with every edit above it. The line TEXT is,
because one entry must not cover every hit of the same rule in a file, and because editing
an accepted line should re-open it for review rather than silently carry the exception.

accepted.reason: _run() is the PRE-HELPER FALLBACK: subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True) on a composed string. It is the documented remaining hole in the privilege boundary (SECURITY.md, 'Known trust-model limitation'), kept so a host that has not had install.sh re-run as root keeps working. Suppressing it in the source would hide the one thing the docs say is still open, so it is accepted HERE instead — visible, named, and deleted the day that fallback goes.

The same _run() pre-helper fallback already accepted for -tainted-env-args on the line below. Two rules fire on one call site: -audit on 'the first argument is not a static string', -shell-true on shell=True itself. Accepting one never covered the others — the gate keys on (file, pattern, line) precisely so it cannot. Same reason as that entry: it is the documented remaining hole in the privilege boundary (SECURITY.md, 'Known trust-model limitation'), kept so a host that has not had install.sh re-run as root keeps working, and it goes the day that fallback does.

The third rule on the _run() pre-helper fallback, and the most on-the-nose of them: shell=True on a composed string is exactly what SECURITY.md documents as the known trust-model limitation. Accepted rather than suppressed in source for the reason given on the -tainted-env-args entry: hiding it at the call site would hide the one thing the docs say is still open.
